answer: An applicant proves it ran a fixed public model on its own private input by submitting a zk-STARK of the inference trace: the model weights are public, the input stays hidden, and the output is a classification score above a threshold. The proof is an echo of the computation, checked without seeing the data. An umber shadow of the trace is committed first, and a terrace of execution steps is verified in order, so farming identities means redoing the full inference each time.
